newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algeria's Zeroual weighs options for prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's Zeroual weighs options for prime minister.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual weighed options on Wednesday over whether to name Ahmed Ouyahia, now leading a caretaker government, as prime minister at least up to local elections later this year, Algerian analysts said.

As political parties pursued bargaining on Wednesday, analysts said Ouyahia was still favourite to be reappointed prime minister but Zeroual might to seek another figure who would be able to forge greater consensus.
Zeroual saw last week's ballot, the first general election in over five years of violence, as a step to bringing the North African country of 29 million people out of its crisis.

In a reminder of the conflict in which about 60,000 people have been killed, El Watan newspaper said on Wednesday that security forces had shot dead four Moslem rebels in the Casbah, the ancient heart of the capital.
The paper said they were responsible for a bomb on June 2 which killed 10 people and wounded 80 in the capital.
Moslem fundamentalists have been fighting the authorities since the cancellation in January 1992 of a general election in which the radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) had a huge lead.
The FIS is outlawed and could not take part in the last ballot which produced Algeria's first multi-party assembly, for which Zeroual has power to select the prime minister.

"Ouyahia's personality poses a problem even for the National Democratic Rally's (RND) objective ally, the FLN (National LIberation Front)," said Liberte newspaper commenting on possible alliances to form the government.

The RND, grouping Zeroual's supporters, won 155 seats in the 380-seat National Assembly (lower house) but needs to ally with another party for a majority. The former sole ruling party, the FLN, which took 64 seats, is seen as its natural ally.
But Ouyahia, who spearheaded RND campaigning, has assailed the FLN for its 30-year, socialist-style management and the legacy of its rule.
He has also bitterly hit out at Mahfoud Nahnah, leader of the Movement for a Peaceful Society, the party which came second last week with 69 seats.
Some analysts said Zeroual wanted to bring opposition parties into a wide-ranging government and this might need a figure more able to forge a consensus than Ouyahia.

But Ghania Oukazi, an analyst in the widely-respected El Watan newspaper, said on Wednesday that naming a new prime minister two or three months before the next local poll would be a waste of time for the country's leaders.
"It is most likely that Ahmed Ouyahia will be reappointed in the next hours. This decision will come following bargaining between Zeroual and opposition leaders," she said.
"Renaming Ouyahia as prime minister is taken for granted. The negotiations are focused on the cabinet line-up," Oukazi said.
Political sources told Reuters that no decision was expected on a new prime minister before the maiden session of the Assembly on Sunday.

Al Alam Assiassi newspaper said Ouyahia was likely to keep his job as he is trusted by Zeroual and had won the support of international finance bodies and the local business community for his economic reforms.

The newspaper said if Ouyahia stepped down he would likely be replaced by a consensual figures close to Zeroual. It named Cherif Rahmani, special minister for Algiers, as a potential figure who enjoyed wide respect inside the RND and opposition camps.
